pk_sampling.domain: Phase 1 two-period food-effect crossover PK sampling log: 24 subjects in 4 dose cohorts, 13 timepoints per period

errors.proof: Cohort B is dosed 50 mg on every other row, including the other 25 rows of S-1010; this one row of the same subject and period says 100 mg.
The 12 h sample's Actual_h 1.75 is earlier than the same profile's 8 h sample (7.91); elapsed time after dose must increase along a profile, and its Deviation_min is far outside every window.
Dosed at clock hour 8.25 and drawn 24.46 h later the sample falls on the next day, yet Sample_Date equals Dose_Date 2026-05-05.
0.0459 is below the LLOQ of 0.5 ng/mL yet BLQ says N; the neighbouring timepoints of the profile put it near 45.9 ng/mL, i.e. the value was entered in ug/mL.
Every other Deviation_min is (Actual_h - Nominal_h) * 60; this cell multiplies by 6, so the deviation is a tenth of the real one and still looks plausible.
Period 1 pre-dose sample: the subject has never been dosed, so it must be below the LLOQ like every other Period 1 pre-dose row; 3.8 ng/mL is reported.
The other 12 rows of S-1014 period 2 share one later Dose_Date; this row carries the period 1 date 2026-04-13, 14 days before, which also contradicts its own Sample_Date and Actual_h.

traps.why: Pre-dose sample drawn 1.45 h (87 min) before dosing: an extreme but inside the 90 min pre-dose window; a negative elapsed time is how every pre-dose row is written.
Period 2 pre-dose level of 0.62 ng/mL, just above the LLOQ, is under 5% of the subject's period 1 Cmax (1610.0), the accepted limit for a crossover; not an error.
A late draw outside its 30 min window, recorded with its true time and a documented deviation comment; the N is correct.
This period was dosed at clock hour 13.5, so the 12 h sample falls after midnight and its Sample_Date is correctly the next day, unlike other subjects' 12 h samples.
The cohort C Cmax far above the others belongs to a high-exposure subject whose whole profile, in both periods, is about 2.4 times the cohort; a consistent profile, not a typo.

fa_depreciation.domain: Fixed-asset depreciation schedule, FY2020-FY2026, one row per asset and year, with the depreciation journal (Dr expense / Cr accumulated depreciation)

errors.proof: Opening_Accum_Dep is =Closing-Depreciation of its own row while Closing is =Opening+Depreciation: a circular reference that shows a plausible number; every other opening is the previous year's closing (=R[-1]C[2]).
Depreciation expense on a straight-line asset cannot be negative; -27857.05 is typed over the formula, which gives 27857.05, and it pulls accumulated depreciation down.
The asset's other rows give Cost 20220.27; this row gives 20.22 (keyed in thousands), so its depreciation and NBV are a thousandth of the real ones.
A Plant & Machinery depreciation (Dr 6120) is credited to 1640, the Vehicles accumulated depreciation account; every other row of the class and of this asset credits 1620.
First year in service for 4 months, but the formula drops *Months/12 and charges a full year; a plausible amount that every other straight-line row prorates.
In service 2024-08-15: under the full-month convention every other first year counts 5 months from that month to December; this row claims 12 and over-depreciates.
FA-10025 was disposed in FY2025 (proceeds and gain on that row), yet a FY2026 row still charges depreciation on it.
Final year of a 5-year vehicle: the formula lost its MIN cap and charges a full year, so accumulated depreciation passes Cost - Salvage and NBV falls below the salvage value.

traps.why: Land is never depreciated: no method, no life, no accounts and a zero charge are correct, and NBV stays at cost.
IT Equipment uses double-declining balance, a second formula the whole class shares; it charges on cost less opening accumulated depreciation, not straight line.
Sold below its NBV, so the disposal is a loss: a negative gain is the right sign.
A 5-year vehicle in service since February 2020 is fully depreciated to its salvage value; it stays on the register with a zero charge.
Two identical forklifts bought the same day at the same price: their schedules repeat row for row under two asset IDs, which is correct.

landed_cost.domain: US import landed-cost sheet: multi-currency invoices, weight-based freight allocation, ad valorem and specific duties, one row per invoice line

errors.proof: Every other EUR line shipped 2026-01-30, including the rest of this shipment, uses 1.0909; this line uses 1.099 (two digits swapped).
Every other GLV-6110 line weighs the same kg per unit; this one is 2.2046 times that (456.4 for 207.0 kg: pounds), and it takes too much of the shipment's freight.
The weight total in this line's allocation leaves out the shipment's last line, so its share is too big and the shipment's allocations add up to more than its freight.
HS 8481.80 is ad valorem (AV 0.02): duty is Line_Value_USD x rate, but this cell multiplies the rate by the gross weight, as only SPEC_KG lines do.
An import line cannot ship a negative quantity (-1500) with a positive gross weight; line value and landed cost turn negative while the landed unit cost still looks normal.
The shipment's other lines carry freight 2356.99; this line says 3256.99, so its allocation and the shipment total no longer reconcile.
The shipment's other lines were entered 2026-02-04; this line says 2026-04-02 (day and month swapped), outside the 15-day customs entry window around arrival 2026-02-02.
Landed cost is goods value + allocated freight + duty on every other line; this formula leaves out the freight and gives a plausible, too low number.

traps.why: Mexican-origin goods qualify for USMCA: a zero duty rate on an HS code that is dutiable from every other origin is correct.
Wine (HS 2204.21) pays a specific duty per kg, a second formula its whole category uses: duty = weight x 0.063 USD/kg, not 6.3% of value.
A pre-arrival customs entry, filed 2 days before the vessel arrives: allowed, so an Entry_Date before Arrival_Date is valid here.
Two purchase orders for the same SKU, quantity and price consolidated in one container: two identical lines under different line numbers.
One machining centre at EUR 186,400 weighing 4,200 kg: an extreme price and weight that take most of the shipment freight, all genuine.

ev_mass_rollup.domain: Multi-level BOM mass and centre-of-gravity roll-up for three electric utility vehicle variants, with alternates and effectivity dates

errors.proof: FST-M8X25 weighs 0.0142 kg on every other row of the BOM; here 14.2 (grams), which inflates its sub-assembly's roll-up.
The sub-assembly's mass formula adds its own Ext_Mass_kg, which is computed from this same cell: a circular reference still showing the old, plausible total.
A part cannot have negative mass (arms may be negative, masses never); the minus sign lowers its parent's roll-up and shifts its centre of gravity.
By its level the row sits under SA-72383, which rolls it up, but Parent_PN says SA-72373, a sibling sub-assembly.
The mass roll-up skips P-44226, a primary, effective child that the same row's CG formulas include, so the mass is too low and the CG is wrong.
Effective_To 2023-04-01 is before Effective_From 2024-09-01; the replacement part on the next row starts 2025-04-01, the real end date.
The sub-assembly's mass is a typed number, not the sum of its effective children, and it is 3% above what they add up to.
NUT-M8 (Nyloc nut M8) is counted in EA: 16.5 pieces cannot be fitted; only length items (UoM M) take fractions.

traps.why: The X datum is the front bumper face: the tow eye stands 38 mm ahead of it, so a negative arm and a negative moment are correct.
An alternate source (Alt_Priority 2) is listed for purchasing but not built in, so its mass is rightly left out of the parent roll-up.
The sheet holds three vehicle variants; this is the second top-level item (Level 0), so a blank Parent_PN is correct.
The pack stacks two identical cell modules; the second block repeats the first row for row, only 150 mm higher, which is correct.
A superseded part kept for history with an end date in the past: it is rightly out of the roll-up, and its replacement starts that day on the next row.
Cable is bought by the metre (UoM M): a fractional quantity is correct.
